records.context: This module generalises :func:`spacr.core.reducer_hyperparameter_search`, which already swept UMAP/tSNE + DBSCAN/KMeans parameters and drew the resulting embeddings as a grid of small multiples. That function stays where it is (it still owns the database read + the image-glyph plotting); what lives here is the search machinery it lacked: recorded trials, failed trials that do not abort the sweep, an incremental progress callback, early stopping, reproducible sampling, and — most importantly — an explicit, named scoring criterion instead of an unscored eyeball grid.
records.label: spacr.hyperparam#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module generalises :func:`spacr.core.reducer_hyperparameter_search`, which already swept UMAP/tSNE + DBSCAN/KMeans parameters and drew the resulting embeddings as a grid of small multiples. That function stays where it is (it still owns the database read + the image-glyph plotting); what lives here is the search machinery it lacked: recorded trials, failed trials that do not abort the sweep, an incremental progress callback, early stopping, reproducible sampling, and — most importantly — an explicit, named scoring criterion instead of an unscored eyeball grid.
records.translation: Este módulo generaliza :func:`spacr.core.reducer_hyperparameter_search`, que já varria parâmetros de UMAP/tSNE + DBSCAN/KMeans e desenhava as projeções resultantes como uma grade de pequenos múltiplos. Essa função permanece onde está (ela ainda é responsável pela leitura do banco de dados + a plotagem com glifos de imagem); o que fica aqui é a maquinaria de busca que lhe faltava: tentativas registradas, tentativas com falha que não abortam a varredura, um callback de progresso incremental, parada antecipada, amostragem reprodutível e — o mais importante — um critério de pontuação explícito e nomeado, em vez de uma grade sem pontuação avaliada a olho.

records.context: Three limitations are stated explicitly:
records.label: spacr.hyperparam#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Three limitations are stated explicitly:
records.translation: Três limitações são declaradas explicitamente:

records.context: **UMAP has no ground truth.** There is no measurement that says one embedding is correct and another is wrong. Every criterion here (trustworthiness, continuity, silhouette) rewards a *different* property, and they routinely disagree about which ``n_neighbors``/``min_dist`` wins. The scores are an aid for ranking a panel of embeddings you then look at; they are not a verdict. Anything that prints "best embedding" without naming the criterion is misleading, so :func:`format_search` always names it and always prints the caveat.
records.label: spacr.hyperparam#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **UMAP has no ground truth.** There is no measurement that says one embedding is correct and another is wrong. Every criterion here (trustworthiness, continuity, silhouette) rewards a *different* property, and they routinely disagree about which ``n_neighbors``/``min_dist`` wins. The scores are an aid for ranking a panel of embeddings you then look at; they are not a verdict. Anything that prints "best embedding" without naming the criterion is misleading, so :func:`format_search` always names it and always prints the caveat.
records.translation: **O UMAP não tem verdade de referência.** Não há medida que diga que uma projeção está correta e outra errada. Cada critério aqui (confiabilidade, continuidade, silhueta) recompensa uma propriedade *diferente*, e eles frequentemente discordam sobre qual ``n_neighbors``/``min_dist`` vence. As pontuações ajudam a ordenar um painel de projeções que você depois examina; não são um veredito. Qualquer coisa que imprima "best embedding" (melhor projeção) sem nomear o critério é enganosa, por isso :func:`format_search` sempre o nomeia e sempre imprime a ressalva.

records.context: **Selecting on the test split leaks.** :func:`cv_search` scores every trial on cross-validation folds, never on test, and refuses to execute if a caller hands it folds that touch the held-out test indices. It defaults to *grouped* folds (``group_by='well'``) and reuses :func:`spacr.io.make_cv_folds` — extracted image regions from one microplate sample position share focus, illumination and seeding density, so an ungrouped search picks the model that memorised microplate sample positions and reports an inflated score.
records.label: spacr.hyperparam#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Selecting on the test split leaks.** :func:`cv_search` scores every trial on cross-validation folds, never on test, and refuses to run if a caller hands it folds that touch the held-out test indices. It defaults to *grouped* folds (``group_by='well'``) and reuses :func:`spacr.io.make_cv_folds` — crops from one well share focus, illumination and seeding density, so an ungrouped search picks the model that memorised wells and reports an inflated score.
records.translation: **Selecionar na partição de teste vaza informação.** :func:`cv_search` pontua cada tentativa em dobras de validação cruzada, nunca no teste, e se recusa a executar se um chamador lhe entregar dobras que tocam os índices de teste reservados. Por padrão, usa dobras *agrupadas* (``group_by='well'``) e reutiliza :func:`spacr.io.make_cv_folds` — recortes de um mesmo poço compartilham foco, iluminação e densidade de semeadura, de modo que uma busca sem agrupamento escolhe o modelo que memorizou os poços e informa uma pontuação inflada.

records.context: **A winner is reported with its spread.** When the top ten configurations sit inside the fold-to-fold standard deviation, the hyperparameter did not matter and the "winner" is noise. Every :class:`SearchResult` reports the spread and raises a ``within_noise`` flag when that is what happened.
records.label: spacr.hyperparam#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A winner is reported with its spread.** When the top ten configurations sit inside the fold-to-fold standard deviation, the hyperparameter did not matter and the "winner" is noise. Every :class:`SearchResult` reports the spread and raises a ``within_noise`` flag when that is what happened.
records.translation: **Um vencedor é informado com sua dispersão.** Quando as dez melhores configurações ficam dentro do desvio padrão entre dobras, o hiperparâmetro não fez diferença e o "winner" (vencedor) é ruído. Todo :class:`SearchResult` informa a dispersão e ativa a flag ``within_noise`` quando foi isso que aconteceu.

records.source: Reuses :func:`spacr.io.make_cv_folds`, the same fold builder ``cross_validation_folds`` drives during training, so a search and the run it configures split the data the same way. Grouping defaults to ``'well'`` because crops from one well share focus, illumination, seeding density and edge effects; letting them straddle a split lets a model recognise the well instead of the phenotype.
records.translation: Reutiliza :func:`spacr.io.make_cv_folds`, o mesmo construtor de dobras que ``cross_validation_folds`` aciona durante o treinamento, de modo que uma busca e a execução que ela configura dividem os dados da mesma forma. O agrupamento padrão é ``'well'`` porque recortes de um mesmo poço compartilham foco, iluminação, densidade de semeadura e efeitos de borda; deixá-los dos dois lados de uma divisão permite que um modelo reconheça o poço em vez do fenótipo.

records.source: Every configuration is fitted once per fold on that fold's training indices and scored on that fold's validation indices; the trial score is the mean across folds and the fold-to-fold standard deviation becomes the noise yardstick for :meth:`SearchResult.within_noise`. Indices listed in ``test_idx`` are removed before the folds are built and are never handed to ``fit_fn`` — selecting a configuration on data reserved for the final estimate makes that estimate meaningless.
records.translation: Cada configuração é ajustada uma vez por dobra, nos índices de treinamento dessa dobra, e pontuada nos índices de validação dela; a pontuação da tentativa é a média entre as dobras, e o desvio padrão entre dobras se torna a régua de ruído de :meth:`SearchResult.within_noise`. records.context: Several statistical distinctions are deliberate.  Guide and gene fits are separate multiple-testing families and receive separate corrections; the nominal ``alpha``, effect-size threshold, and corrected significance cutoff are not interchangeable.  A mixed model reports guide effects as shrunken BLUP predictions without guide p- or q-values, so they must not be read as a second guide significance test.  Diagnostic or report-generation failures do not erase successful scientific output, while an actual regression failure is recorded and then re-raised unchanged so callers cannot mistake it for a completed processing session.

records.source: Several statistical distinctions are deliberate.  Guide and gene fits are separate multiple-testing families and receive separate corrections; the nominal ``alpha``, effect-size threshold, and corrected significance cutoff are not interchangeable.  A mixed model reports guide effects as shrunken BLUP predictions without guide p- or q-values, so they must not be read as a second guide significance test.  Diagnostic or report-generation failures do not erase successful scientific output, while an actual regression failure is recorded and then re-raised unchanged so callers cannot mistake it for a completed run.
records.translation: Várias distinções estatísticas são deliberadas.  Os ajustes por guia e por gene são famílias de testes múltiplos separadas e recebem correções separadas; o ``alpha`` nominal, o limiar de tamanho de efeito e o corte de significância corrigido não são intercambiáveis.  Um modelo misto informa os efeitos de guia como predições BLUP com encolhimento, sem valores p ou q por guia, portanto não devem ser lidos como um segundo teste de significância por guia.  Falhas de diagnóstico ou de geração de relatórios não apagam resultados científicos bem-sucedidos, enquanto uma falha real da regressão é registrada e depois propagada novamente sem alteração, para que os chamadores não possam confundi-la com uma execução concluída.

records.context: **These are not valid frequentist p-values for a penalised fit**, and the two callers that reach them know it in different ways. The standard error is the unpenalised ``rse * sqrt(diag((X'X)^-1))`` while the coefficient it is divided into has been shrunk, so the test is mis-specified. The direction of the error is the one that matters here and it is the safe one: the penalty shrinks the numerator and inflates the residual in the denominator, so the statistic is too small and the p-value too large. A penalised fit under-detects here; it does not manufacture hits.

records.source: Centring gives the intercept a meaning. A fitted intercept is the response where every predictor is zero, which on a screen design is a well with no guide in it -- a point that does not exist. Centred on the negative controls, the intercept is the control level, and every coefficient reads directly as "this far above or below the controls".
records.translation: A centralização dá significado ao intercepto. Um intercepto ajustado é a resposta quando todos os preditores são zero, o que, em um delineamento de triagem, é um poço sem nenhum guia -- um ponto que não existe. Centralizado nos controles negativos, o intercepto é o nível dos controles, e cada coeficiente se lê diretamente como "this far above or below the controls" (tanto acima ou abaixo dos controles).

records.source: Fit a mixed model with guides nested within genes.
records.translation: Ajusta um modelo misto com guias aninhados em genes.

records.context: The model treats genes as fixed effects and guides as random effects nested within genes. In statsmodels notation, ``groups=gene`` supplies the outer random intercept and ``vc_formula={'grna': '0 + C(grna)'}`` supplies the guide-within-gene variance component.
records.label: spacr.ml.fit_mixed_model#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The model treats genes as fixed effects and guides as random effects nested within genes. In statsmodels notation, ``groups=gene`` supplies the outer random intercept and ``vc_formula={'grna': '0 + C(grna)'}`` supplies the guide-within-gene variance component.
records.translation: O modelo trata os genes como efeitos fixos e os guias como efeitos aleatórios aninhados em genes. Na notação do statsmodels, ``groups=gene`` fornece o intercepto aleatório externo e ``vc_formula={'grna': '0 + C(grna)'}`` fornece o componente de variância de guia dentro de gene.

records.context: A blockable ``screenID`` supplied by :func:`prepare_formula` remains a fixed effect. With only two screen levels, a random screen variance would be estimated from one degree of freedom. The laboratory microplate is not nested within the screen because laboratory microplate position is already represented by the row and column structure. Single-screen data omit the constant screen term to avoid a rank-deficient design.
records.label: spacr.ml.fit_mixed_model#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A blockable ``screenID`` supplied by :func:`prepare_formula` remains a fixed effect. With only two screen levels, a random screen variance would be estimated from one degree of freedom. The plate is not nested within the screen because plate position is already represented by the row and column structure. Single-screen data omit the constant screen term to avoid a rank-deficient design.
records.translation: Um ``screenID`` bloqueável fornecido por :func:`prepare_formula` permanece como efeito fixo. Com apenas dois níveis de triagem, uma variância aleatória de triagem seria estimada a partir de um único grau de liberdade. A placa não é aninhada na triagem porque a posição na placa já está representada pela estrutura de linhas e colunas. Dados de uma única triagem omitem o termo constante de triagem para evitar um delineamento com posto deficiente.

records.context: dependent_variable : str Name of the response column. random_row_column_effects : bool, default=False Reserve ``plateID``, ``rowID`` and ``columnID`` for the grouping and variance-component structure in :func:`fit_mixed_model` instead of adding them as fixed effects. block_screen : bool, default=False Add ``screenID`` as a fixed effect. Use :func:`screen_is_blockable` before enabling this for user data. level : {'grna', 'gene'}, default='grna' Resolution represented by the formula. ``'grna'`` uses ``fraction:grna`` and ``'gene'`` uses ``gene_fraction:gene``. intercept : {'fitted', 'zero', 'control', 'value'}, default='fitted' What the intercept is. ``'fitted'`` estimates it. ``'zero'`` takes it out of the design, so the fit passes through the origin and a coefficient is a whole predicted score rather than a departure from a baseline. ``'control'`` keeps the term and is completed by the caller, which centres the response on the negative controls first -- the intercept is then the control level by construction. ``'value'`` suppresses the term as well, because the caller has shifted the response by a number the user gave and the intercept is pinned at exactly that number. model_plate_position : bool, default=True Include laboratory microplate position in the model. With ``random_row_column_effects=False`` it is included as fixed laboratory microplate, row, and column terms; with ``random_row_column_effects=True`` laboratory microplate supplies the grouping variable and row/column are variance components. New application settings default to ``False`` even though this helper retains ``True`` for API compatibility.
records.label: spacr.ml.prepare_formula#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: dependent_variable : str Name of the response column. random_row_column_effects : bool, default=False Reserve ``plateID``, ``rowID`` and ``columnID`` for the grouping and variance-component structure in :func:`fit_mixed_model` instead of adding them as fixed effects. block_screen : bool, default=False Add ``screenID`` as a fixed effect. Use :func:`screen_is_blockable` before enabling this for user data. level : {'grna', 'gene'}, default='grna' Resolution represented by the formula. ``'grna'`` uses ``fraction:grna`` and ``'gene'`` uses ``gene_fraction:gene``. intercept : {'fitted', 'zero', 'control', 'value'}, default='fitted' What the intercept is. ``'fitted'`` estimates it. ``'zero'`` takes it out of the design, so the fit passes through the origin and a coefficient is a whole predicted score rather than a departure from a baseline. ``'control'`` keeps the term and is completed by the caller, which centres the response on the negative controls first -- the intercept is then the control level by construction. ``'value'`` suppresses the term as well, because the caller has shifted the response by a number the user gave and the intercept is pinned at exactly that number. model_plate_position : bool, default=True Include plate position in the model. With ``random_row_column_effects=False`` it is included as fixed plate, row, and column terms; with ``random_row_column_effects=True`` plate supplies the grouping variable and row/column are variance components. New application settings default to ``False`` even though this helper retains ``True`` for API compatibility.
records.translation: dependent_variable : str Nome da coluna de resposta. random_row_column_effects : bool, default=False Reserva ``plateID``, ``rowID`` e ``columnID`` para a estrutura de agrupamento e de componentes de variância em :func:`fit_mixed_model`, em vez de adicioná-los como efeitos fixos. block_screen : bool, default=False Adiciona ``screenID`` como efeito fixo. Use :func:`screen_is_blockable` antes de ativar isto para dados do usuário. level : {'grna', 'gene'}, default='grna' Resolução representada pela fórmula. ``'grna'`` usa ``fraction:grna`` e ``'gene'`` usa ``gene_fraction:gene``. intercept : {'fitted', 'zero', 'control', 'value'}, default='fitted' O que é o intercepto. ``'fitted'`` o estima. ``'zero'`` o retira do delineamento, de modo que o ajuste passa pela origem e um coeficiente é uma pontuação prevista inteira, e não um desvio em relação a uma linha de base. ``'control'`` mantém o termo e é completado pelo chamador, que primeiro centraliza a resposta nos controles negativos -- o intercepto é então o nível dos controles por construção. ``'value'`` também suprime o termo, porque o chamador deslocou a resposta por um número fornecido pelo usuário e o intercepto fica fixado exatamente nesse número. model_plate_position : bool, default=True Inclui a posição na placa no modelo. Com ``random_row_column_effects=False``, ela é incluída como termos fixos de placa, linha e coluna; com ``random_row_column_effects=True``, a placa fornece a variável de agrupamento e linha/coluna são componentes de variância. As novas configurações do aplicativo usam ``False`` por padrão, embora esta função auxiliar mantenha ``True`` por compatibilidade da API.

They are not pooled because they are not independent -- same microplate sample positions, and the gene regressor is the sum of the guide regressors -- and doubling the family size would reduce power without added protection. :func:`perform_regression` applies the correction per level and writes ``results_grna.csv`` and ``results_gene.csv``.

records.source: Two fits give two tables and two corrections. Each fit is its own multiple-testing family and is corrected within itself. They are not pooled because they are not independent -- same wells, and the gene regressor is the sum of the guide regressors -- and doubling the family size would reduce power without added protection. :func:`perform_regression` applies the correction per level and writes ``results_grna.csv`` and ``results_gene.csv``.
records.translation: Dois ajustes geram duas tabelas e duas correções. Cada ajuste é sua própria família de testes múltiplos e é corrigido internamente. Eles não são agrupados porque não são independentes -- os mesmos poços, e o regressor do gene é a soma dos regressores dos guias --, e dobrar o tamanho da família reduziria o poder sem proteção adicional. :func:`perform_regression` aplica a correção por nível e grava ``results_grna.csv`` e ``results_gene.csv``.

records.context: A per-well positive count is not comparable between microplate sample positions of different size: ``process_scores`` sums the response for the count models, so a well of 2000 cells contributes roughly four times the count of a well of 500 at the identical underlying rate. Modelling that count without ``offset(log(Ntotal))`` asks the covariates to explain well size, and any covariate correlated with it comes back as a hit. Measured on a 400-well simulation with a nuisance covariate that drives well size and nothing else, and a true rate coefficient of +1.5: without the offset the nuisance term came back at +1.88 with p = 0, ahead of the real effect; with it, +0.002 with p = 0.90.
records.label: spacr.ml.regression_model._poisson_offset#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A per-well positive count is not comparable between wells of different size: ``process_scores`` sums the response for the count models, so a well of 2000 cells contributes roughly four times the count of a well of 500 at the identical underlying rate. Modelling that count without ``offset(log(Ntotal))`` asks the covariates to explain well size, and any covariate correlated with it comes back as a hit. Measured on a 400-well simulation with a nuisance covariate that drives well size and nothing else, and a true rate coefficient of +1.5: without the offset the nuisance term came back at +1.88 with p = 0, ahead of the real effect; with it, +0.002 with p = 0.90.
records.translation: Uma contagem positiva por poço não é comparável entre poços de tamanhos diferentes: ``process_scores`` soma a resposta para os modelos de contagem, de modo que um poço de 2000 células contribui com aproximadamente quatro vezes a contagem de um poço de 500 com a mesma taxa subjacente. Modelar essa contagem sem ``offset(log(Ntotal))`` pede às covariáveis que expliquem o tamanho do poço, e qualquer covariável correlacionada com ele volta como hit. Medido em uma simulação de 400 poços com uma covariável de incômodo que determina o tamanho do poço e nada mais, e um coeficiente de taxa verdadeiro de +1.5: sem o offset, o termo de incômodo voltou com +1.88 e p = 0, à frente do efeito real; com ele, +0.002 e p = 0.90.

records.context: Constant columns are passed through unchanged. ``MinMaxScaler`` maps a column with zero range to all-zeros, and patsy's intercept is exactly such a column, so scaling a design matrix used to silently delete its intercept: statsmodels then fitted a model through the origin and still printed an ``Intercept`` row, of 0.000, in the summary. Every coefficient in that fit absorbs the mean it can no longer estimate.
records.label: spacr.ml.scale_variables#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Constant columns are passed through unchanged. ``MinMaxScaler`` maps a column with zero range to all-zeros, and patsy's intercept is exactly such a column, so scaling a design matrix used to silently delete its intercept: statsmodels then fitted a model through the origin and still printed an ``Intercept`` row, of 0.000, in the summary. Every coefficient in that fit absorbs the mean it can no longer estimate.
records.translation: Colunas constantes são repassadas sem alteração. ``MinMaxScaler`` mapeia uma coluna com amplitude zero para só zeros, e o intercepto do patsy é exatamente uma coluna assim, de modo que escalonar uma matriz de delineamento apagava silenciosamente seu intercepto: o statsmodels então ajustava um modelo passando pela origem e ainda imprimia uma linha ``Intercept``, de 0.000, no resumo. Cada coeficiente desse ajuste absorve a média que não pode mais estimar.

records.context: Pairwise tests are chosen independently by :func:`spacr.figures.stats.compare`. Student's t, Welch's t, or Mann-Whitney U is used according to the normality and equal-variance checks; an underpowered assumption check selects the rank test. records.label: spacr.plot.create_grouped_plot#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Pairwise tests are chosen independently by :func:`spacr.figures.stats.compare`. Student's t, Welch's t, or Mann-Whitney U is used according to the normality and equal-variance checks; an underpowered assumption check selects the rank test. When at least three groups jointly pass normality, Tukey HSD rows are added.
records.translation: Os testes par a par são escolhidos de forma independente por :func:`spacr.figures.stats.compare`. Usa-se t de Student, t de Welch ou U de Mann-Whitney conforme as verificações de normalidade e de igualdade de variâncias; uma verificação de pressupostos com poder insuficiente seleciona o teste de postos. Quando pelo menos três grupos passam juntos na normalidade, são adicionadas linhas de Tukey HSD.

records.context: The ``'jitter_box'`` default is a statistical choice, not a presentation preference: it shows the observations and their distribution instead of reducing each group to a mean bar. Two groups can have the same mean while having different spreads. The box summarizes the distribution; the jitter stays because the points are the evidence.
records.label: spacr.plot.create_grouped_plot#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The ``'jitter_box'`` default is a statistical choice, not a presentation preference: it shows the observations and their distribution instead of reducing each group to a mean bar. Two groups can have the same mean while having different spreads. The box summarizes the distribution; the jitter stays because the points are the evidence.
records.translation: O padrão ``'jitter_box'`` é uma escolha estatística, e não uma preferência de apresentação: ele mostra as observações e sua distribuição, em vez de reduzir cada grupo a uma barra de média. Dois grupos podem ter a mesma média e dispersões diferentes. O box plot resume a distribuição; o jitter permanece porque os pontos são a evidência.

records.context: The grid is **read off the data**. It used to be pinned to ``r1..r16`` by ``c1..c27``, so every microplate sample position of a 1536 laboratory microplate past row P or past column 27 fell outside the ``Categorical``, became NaN, and was dropped by the groupby — measured, in the database, and absent from the figure with nothing said. Rows and columns now go through :func:`spacr.plate_qc.parse_row_label` / ``parse_column_label`` (which is :mod:`spacr.schema`'s letter walk, so ``AA``…``AF`` and beyond are real rows), and the axes span exactly the microplate sample positions present: a 96 laboratory microplate is still 8x12 and a 384 still 16x24, because nothing is padded out to the largest format that exists.
records.label: spacr.plot.generate_plate_heatmap#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The grid is **read off the data**. It used to be pinned to ``r1..r16`` by ``c1..c27``, so every well of a 1536 plate past row P or past column 27 fell outside the ``Categorical``, became NaN, and was dropped by the groupby — measured, in the database, and absent from the figure with nothing said. Rows and columns now go through :func:`spacr.plate_qc.parse_row_label` / ``parse_column_label`` (which is :mod:`spacr.schema`'s letter walk, so ``AA``…``AF`` and beyond are real rows), and the axes span exactly the wells present: a 96 plate is still 8x12 and a 384 still 16x24, because nothing is padded out to the largest format that exists.
records.translation: A grade é **lida a partir dos dados**. Antes ela era fixada em ``r1..r16`` por ``c1..c27``, de modo que todo poço de uma placa de 1536 além da linha P ou da coluna 27 ficava fora do ``Categorical``, virava NaN e era descartado pelo groupby — medido, no banco de dados, e ausente da figura sem nenhum aviso. Agora as linhas e as colunas passam por :func:`spacr.plate_qc.parse_row_label` / ``parse_column_label`` (que é o percurso de letras de :mod:`spacr.schema`, de modo que ``AA``…``AF`` e além são linhas reais), e os eixos cobrem exatamente os poços presentes: uma placa de 96 continua 8x12 e uma de 384 continua 16x24, porque nada é preenchido até o maior formato existente.

records.source: THE CONTRACT IS THAT NOTHING SURVIVES IT. Every artist touched is restored in a ``finally``, so a user watching a plot while it saves must not see it flash and the figure is byte-identical afterwards -- the own acceptance, and the reason this is a context manager rather than a function that fixes a figure up.
records.translation: O CONTRATO É QUE NADA SOBREVIVE A ELE. Cada artista alterado é restaurado em um ``finally``, de modo que um usuário que observa um gráfico enquanto ele é salvo não pode vê-lo piscar, e a figura fica idêntica byte a byte depois -- esse é o critério de aceitação, e o motivo de isto ser um gerenciador de contexto, e não uma função que conserta uma figura.

records.source: WHAT MOVES: an illegible ground becomes the page; illegible chrome becomes the ink; an illegible GRID becomes a faint print grey rather than the ink, because a grid repainted in the ink is a cage over the data.
records.translation: O QUE MUDA: um fundo ilegível vira a página; elementos de moldura ilegíveis viram a tinta; uma GRADE ilegível vira um cinza claro de impressão, e não a tinta, porque uma grade repintada com a tinta é uma jaula sobre os dados.

records.context: Outcome of the normality check, which selects the family of test: True runs Tukey HSD, False runs Dunn's test with an automatically chosen p-adjustment. It only matters when post-hoc testing runs at all — see ``unique_groups``. It must be the verdict :meth:`perform_normality_tests` returned, which is :func:`spacr.figures.stats.check_normality`'s. A hand-computed one puts the omnibus test and the pairwise tests on different footing — Kruskal-Wallis across the groups followed by Tukey between them is two different assumptions about one dataset — and it is how the statistical detection sensitivity floor gets bypassed: three replicates buy Dunn's, not Tukey.

records.source: Outcome of the normality check, which selects the family of test: True runs Tukey HSD, False runs Dunn's test with an automatically chosen p-adjustment. It only matters when post-hoc testing runs at all — see ``unique_groups``. It must be the verdict :meth:`perform_normality_tests` returned, which is :func:`spacr.figures.stats.check_normality`'s. A hand-computed one puts the omnibus test and the pairwise tests on different footing — Kruskal-Wallis across the groups followed by Tukey between them is two different assumptions about one dataset — and it is how the power floor gets bypassed: three replicates buy Dunn's, not Tukey.
records.translation: Resultado da verificação de normalidade, que seleciona a família do teste: True executa Tukey HSD, False executa o teste de Dunn com um ajuste de p escolhido automaticamente. Só importa quando o teste post hoc chega a ser executado — consulte ``unique_groups``. Deve ser o veredito que :meth:`perform_normality_tests` retornou, que é o de :func:`spacr.figures.stats.check_normality`. Um veredito calculado à mão coloca o teste global e os testes par a par em bases diferentes — Kruskal-Wallis entre os grupos seguido de Tukey entre eles são duas suposições diferentes sobre um mesmo conjunto de dados —, e é assim que o piso de potência estatística é contornado: três réplicas dão direito ao teste de Dunn, não ao de Tukey.

records.context: Why this exists
records.label: spacr.seg_qc#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Why this exists
records.translation: Por que isto existe

records.context: ``size outliers`` The fraction of objects whose equivalent diameter falls outside ``median ± seg_qc_outlier_mad * 1.4826 * MAD``. Median and MAD, not mean and standard deviation: five pieces of debris inflate a standard deviation until nothing is an outlier any more, which is the exact case this check exists to catch (``tests/test_seg_qc.py`` contrasts the two). *k* = 5 is deliberately loose — real size distributions are lognormal and heavier tailed than Gaussian, so 3 sigma flags a few percent of a perfectly good field. The flag fires when more than ``seg_qc_outlier_fraction`` (0.15) of objects are out there. Heavy tails, mixed populations and segmentation defects can all trigger it; the flag does not identify which is present. Border objects are excluded from every size statistic, exactly as ``diameter._region_diameters`` excludes them, because a truncated object's area is underestimated.
records.label: spacr.seg_qc#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``size outliers`` The fraction of objects whose equivalent diameter falls outside ``median ± seg_qc_outlier_mad * 1.4826 * MAD``. Median and MAD, not mean and standard deviation: five pieces of debris inflate a standard deviation until nothing is an outlier any more, which is the exact case this check exists to catch (``tests/test_seg_qc.py`` contrasts the two). *k* = 5 is deliberately loose — real size distributions are lognormal and heavier tailed than Gaussian, so 3 sigma flags a few percent of a perfectly good field. The flag fires when more than ``seg_qc_outlier_fraction`` (0.15) of objects are out there. Heavy tails, mixed populations and segmentation defects can all trigger it; the flag does not identify which is present. Border objects are excluded from every size statistic, exactly as ``diameter._region_diameters`` excludes them, because a truncated object's area is underestimated.
records.translation: ``size outliers`` A fração de objetos cujo diâmetro equivalente fica fora de ``median ± seg_qc_outlier_mad * 1.4826 * MAD``. Mediana e MAD, e não média e desvio padrão: cinco fragmentos de detritos inflam um desvio padrão até que nada mais seja atípico, que é exatamente o caso que esta verificação existe para detectar (``tests/test_seg_qc.py`` contrasta os dois). *k* = 5 é deliberadamente folgado — distribuições reais de tamanho são lognormais e têm caudas mais pesadas que a gaussiana, então 3 sigma sinalizaria alguns por cento de um campo perfeitamente bom. A flag dispara quando mais de ``seg_qc_outlier_fraction`` (0.15) dos objetos estão fora desse intervalo. Caudas pesadas, populações mistas e defeitos de segmentação podem dispará-la; a flag não identifica qual deles está presente. Objetos de borda são excluídos de todas as estatísticas de tamanho, exatamente como ``diameter._region_diameters`` os exclui, porque a área de um objeto truncado é subestimada.

records.context: ``empty / near-empty fields`` Zero objects is a failure. Fewer than ``seg_qc_min_objects`` (10) is a warning and suppresses the per-microscope field of view robust statistics, because below ten objects a MAD is not a reliable spread estimate — the same threshold at which diameter.py collapses its confidence two levels. If the *laboratory microplate* median is also below that floor (a low-MOI pathogen channel, say), empty microscope fields of view are demoted to a warning: that is a property of the assay, not of the microscope field of view.
records.label: spacr.seg_qc#12
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``empty / near-empty fields`` Zero objects is a failure. Fewer than ``seg_qc_min_objects`` (10) is a warning and suppresses the per-field robust statistics, because below ten objects a MAD is not a reliable spread estimate — the same threshold at which diameter.py collapses its confidence two levels. If the *plate* median is also below that floor (a low-MOI pathogen channel, say), empty fields are demoted to a warning: that is a property of the assay, not of the field.
records.translation: ``empty / near-empty fields`` Zero objetos é uma falha. Menos de ``seg_qc_min_objects`` (10) é um aviso e suprime as estatísticas robustas por campo, porque abaixo de dez objetos a MAD não é uma estimativa confiável de dispersão — o mesmo limiar em que diameter.py reduz sua confiança em dois níveis. Se a mediana da *placa* também estiver abaixo desse piso (um canal de patógeno com MOI baixo, por exemplo), os campos vazios são rebaixados a aviso: isso é uma propriedade do ensaio, e não do campo.

records.label: spacr.seg_qc#14
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``FieldQC`` One field's verdict: counts, flags, the numbers behind them, severity. ``score_field(mask, object_type, **thresholds)`` Score one label image, with no plate context. ``score_masks(source, object_type, ...)`` Score a folder of ``.npy`` masks, a 3-D stack or a list of 2-D masks, then add the plate-relative flags. ``summarize_qc(field_qcs)`` Plate-level rollup: verdict, counts per severity, the failing field names. ``format_scorecard(field_qcs)`` The printable card. ``write_scorecard(field_qcs, dst, object_type)`` ``<dst>/qc/segmentation_qc_<object_type>.csv``, one row per field. ``run_segmentation_qc(...)`` What :mod:`spacr.object` calls: score, write, print, honour ``seg_qc``. ``thresholds_from_settings(settings)`` Pull the ``seg_qc_*`` knobs out of a settings dict.
records.translation: ``FieldQC`` O veredito de um campo: contagens, flags, os números por trás delas, gravidade. ``score_field(mask, object_type, **thresholds)`` Pontua uma imagem de rótulos, sem contexto da placa. ``score_masks(source, object_type, ...)`` Pontua uma pasta de máscaras ``.npy``, uma pilha 3-D ou uma lista de máscaras 2-D e depois acrescenta as flags relativas à placa. ``summarize_qc(field_qcs)`` Consolidação no nível da placa: veredito, contagens por gravidade, os nomes dos campos com falha. ``format_scorecard(field_qcs)`` O quadro imprimível. ``write_scorecard(field_qcs, dst, object_type)`` ``<dst>/qc/segmentation_qc_<object_type>.csv``, uma linha por campo. ``run_segmentation_qc(...)`` O que :mod:`spacr.object` chama: pontua, grava, imprime, respeita ``seg_qc``. ``thresholds_from_settings(settings)`` Extrai os parâmetros ``seg_qc_*`` de um dict de configurações.

records.source: Everything above runs once, at mask time, and writes a CSV. The second half of this module reads that CSV back and turns it into something a user can act on, without scoring a single mask again:
records.translation: Tudo acima é executado uma vez, no momento das máscaras, e grava um CSV. A segunda metade deste módulo lê esse CSV de volta e o transforma em algo sobre o qual o usuário pode agir, sem pontuar nenhuma máscara de novo:

records.context: This module checks them. It reads the label masks that :mod:`spacr.object` has just written, scores every microscope field of view against a handful of robust statistics, and prints a scorecard naming microscope fields of view that exceed configured thresholds. It changes nothing: ``seg_qc='report'`` (the default) surfaces the flags, it does not silently drop microscope fields of view. Deciding which microscope fields of view to keep is the user's call and it needs the evidence, not a filter.
records.label: spacr.seg_qc#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module checks them. It reads the label masks that :mod:`spacr.object` has just written, scores every field against a handful of robust statistics, and prints a scorecard naming fields that exceed configured thresholds. It changes nothing: ``seg_qc='report'`` (the default) surfaces the flags, it does not silently drop fields. Deciding which fields to keep is the user's call and it needs the evidence, not a filter.
records.translation: Este módulo as verifica. Ele lê as máscaras de rótulos que :mod:`spacr.object` acabou de gravar, pontua cada campo segundo um punhado de estatísticas robustas e imprime um quadro de avaliação que cita os campos que excedem os limiares configurados. Ele não altera nada: ``seg_qc='report'`` (o padrão) exibe as flags, mas não descarta campos silenciosamente. Decidir quais campos manter cabe ao usuário, e isso exige a evidência, não um filtro.

records.context: Design constraint: this executes right after segmentation on every microscope field of view of the laboratory microplate, so it must be cheap. Everything below is ``np.bincount`` on a label image — microseconds per microscope field of view. The one expensive check (the distance-transform cross-check for fusion) runs *only* on microscope fields of view dense enough for fusion to be the explanation, so a healthy laboratory microplate never pays for it. Like :mod:`spacr.diameter`, this module imports **no torch and no cellpose**; this is tested (see ``tests/test_seg_qc.py``).
records.label: spacr.seg_qc#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Design constraint: this runs right after segmentation on every field of the plate, so it must be cheap. Everything below is ``np.bincount`` on a label image — microseconds per field. The one expensive check (the distance-transform cross-check for fusion) runs *only* on fields dense enough for fusion to be the explanation, so a healthy plate never pays for it. Like :mod:`spacr.diameter`, this module imports **no torch and no cellpose**; this is tested (see ``tests/test_seg_qc.py``).
records.translation: Restrição de projeto: isto é executado logo após a segmentação, em todos os campos da placa, por isso precisa ser barato. Tudo abaixo é ``np.bincount`` sobre uma imagem de rótulos — microssegundos por campo. A única verificação cara (a verificação cruzada por transformada de distância para fusões) é executada *apenas* em campos densos o bastante para que a fusão seja a explicação, de modo que uma placa saudável nunca paga por ela. Assim como :mod:`spacr.diameter`, este módulo **não importa torch nem cellpose**; isso é testado (consulte ``tests/test_seg_qc.py``).

When spaCR then measures the same field, :func:`_merge_and_save_to_database` *appends*: the measured rows are added beside the imported ones, in different columns, with nothing in the row to distinguish them, and every downstream ``count_cell`` becomes the sum of two populations.

records.source: ``foreign.run_import`` copies the imported frame into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when the destination is empty, so a project built purely by import is readable by every spaCR tool. When spaCR then measures the same field, :func:`_merge_and_save_to_database` *appends*: the measured rows are added beside the imported ones, in different columns, with nothing in the row to distinguish them, and every downstream ``count_cell`` becomes the sum of two populations.
records.translation: ``foreign.run_import`` copia o quadro de dados importado para a tabela canônica ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` quando o destino está vazio, de modo que um projeto montado apenas por importação possa ser lido por todas as ferramentas do spaCR. Quando o spaCR depois mede o mesmo campo, :func:`_merge_and_save_to_database` *acrescenta*: as linhas medidas são adicionadas ao lado das importadas, em colunas diferentes, sem nada na linha que as distinga, e cada ``count_cell`` posterior passa a ser a soma de duas populações.

records.source: A resume supersedes the copy before measuring (see :func:`spacr.resume.supersede_imported_copies`) or refuses with a message. This exception covers the case without a resume: a direct ``measure_crop`` with ``resume`` off.
records.translation: Uma retomada substitui a cópia antes de medir (consulte :func:`spacr.resume.supersede_imported_copies`) ou recusa com uma mensagem. Esta exceção cobre o caso sem retomada: um ``measure_crop`` direto com ``resume`` desativado.

records.context: Raised only when the copy cannot be released **provably losslessly** -- no ``foreign_<object>`` to check the rows against, a row in the copy with no counterpart in it, a timelapse whose frames the importer never keyed, or a delete that did not act on the rows the count cleared. In each of those cases the field's rows are not written, because a refused write can be re-run and a mixed table cannot be separated again.
records.label: spacr.utils.ImportedCopyNotReleased#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Raised only when the copy cannot be released **provably losslessly** -- no ``foreign_<object>`` to check the rows against, a row in the copy with no counterpart in it, a timelapse whose frames the importer never keyed, or a delete that did not act on the rows the count cleared. In each of those cases the field's rows are not written, because a refused write can be re-run and a mixed table cannot be separated again.
records.translation: Gerada apenas quando a cópia não pode ser liberada de forma **comprovadamente sem perdas** -- não há ``foreign_<object>`` com que conferir as linhas, há uma linha na cópia sem correspondente nele, um lapso de tempo cujos quadros o importador nunca indexou, ou uma exclusão que não atuou sobre as linhas que a contagem liberou. Em cada um desses casos, as linhas do campo não são gravadas, porque uma gravação recusada pode ser executada novamente, e uma tabela misturada não pode ser separada de novo.

records.context: a PIL image or a numpy array. Arrays are used as-is; PIL images are converted first. A 2-D grayscale input is expanded to 3 image data channels via ``cv2.cvtColor``, so every result is RGB even when the input was not -- image data channel count is not preserved. The rotations go through ``cv2``, which expects ``uint8`` or another OpenCV-supported dtype; the final ``Image.fromarray`` likewise rejects the float or 16-bit arrays typical of raw microscopy, so convert to 8-bit before calling. Because 90-degree rotations swap height and width, a non-square input yields images of two different shapes in the same list.

The rotations go through ``cv2``, which expects ``uint8`` or another OpenCV-supported dtype; the final ``Image.fromarray`` likewise rejects the float or 16-bit arrays typical of raw microscopy, so convert to 8-bit before calling. records.translation: uma imagem PIL ou um array do numpy. Arrays são usados como estão; imagens PIL são convertidas primeiro. Como rotações de 90 graus trocam altura e largura, uma entrada não quadrada produz imagens de duas formas diferentes na mesma lista.

A regra em si fica em :func:`spacr.schema.canonical_rename_plan`, que esta função e ``schema.canonicalise_columns`` chamam, para que os dois canonizadores de quadros de dados não possam divergir de novo — e que ignora maiúsculas/minúsculas, porque esses quadros são gravados com ``to_sql`` e o SQLite compara identificadores sem diferenciar maiúsculas de minúsculas.

records.context: Computing the position as ``sorted({nucleus, cell, pathogen, organelle})`` instead agrees with role order only when the roles are in ascending image data channel order. With ``nucleus_channel=2, cell_channel=0, organelle_channel=1`` the stack is ``[2, 0, 1]`` -- raw image data channel 1 sits at position 2 -- while the sorted reading gives position 1, which holds the cell image. Cellpose would then segment organelles on the cell image layer without any warning, and downstream counts and intensities would be measured from the wrong masks.
records.label: spacr.utils.dense_mask_channel_positions#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Computing the position as ``sorted({nucleus, cell, pathogen, organelle})`` instead agrees with role order only when the roles are in ascending channel order. With ``nucleus_channel=2, cell_channel=0, organelle_channel=1`` the stack is ``[2, 0, 1]`` -- raw channel 1 sits at position 2 -- while the sorted reading gives position 1, which holds the cell image. Cellpose would then segment organelles on the cell plane without any warning, and downstream counts and intensities would be measured from the wrong masks.
records.translation: Calcular a posição como ``sorted({nucleus, cell, pathogen, organelle})`` só coincide com a ordem dos papéis quando os papéis estão em ordem crescente de canal. Com ``nucleus_channel=2, cell_channel=0, organelle_channel=1``, a pilha é ``[2, 0, 1]`` -- o canal bruto 1 fica na posição 2 --, enquanto a leitura ordenada dá a posição 1, que contém a imagem de células. O Cellpose então segmentaria as organelas no plano das células sem nenhum aviso, e as contagens e intensidades posteriores seriam medidas a partir das máscaras erradas.

records.source: The two tests are combined with OR, not AND, so this is a two-tailed selection that keeps the extremes and discards the middle. Both comparisons are strict, so a value exactly equal to either threshold is dropped, and so is ``NaN``. Passing an ``upper_threshold`` below ``lower_threshold`` makes the two conditions cover the whole line and nothing is filtered out at all.
records.translation: Os dois testes são combinados com OR, e não com AND, de modo que esta é uma seleção bicaudal que mantém os extremos e descarta o meio. As duas comparações são estritas, então um valor exatamente igual a qualquer um dos limiares é descartado, assim como ``NaN``. Passar um ``upper_threshold`` abaixo de ``lower_threshold`` faz as duas condições cobrirem a reta inteira, e nada é filtrado.

records.context: Parameters: input_csv (str): Path to the input CSV file, read with ``pd.read_csv``. output_csv (str): Path to save the filtered CSV file, written without the index. Its parent directory must already exist -- pandas throws ``OSError`` rather than creating it. column_name (str): Column the two comparisons are applied to. A name that is not in the frame throws ``KeyError``, and a text column throws ``TypeError`` when compared against a numeric threshold. upper_threshold (float): Rows strictly greater than this are retained. lower_threshold (float): Rows strictly less than this are retained too; everything between the two bounds is discarded.
records.label: spacr.utils.filter_and_save_csv#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Parameters: input_csv (str): Path to the input CSV file, read with ``pd.read_csv``. output_csv (str): Path to save the filtered CSV file, written without the index. Its parent directory must already exist -- pandas raises ``OSError`` rather than creating it. column_name (str): Column the two comparisons are applied to. A name that is not in the frame raises ``KeyError``, and a text column raises ``TypeError`` when compared against a numeric threshold. upper_threshold (float): Rows strictly greater than this are retained. lower_threshold (float): Rows strictly less than this are retained too; everything between the two bounds is discarded.
records.translation: Parâmetros: input_csv (str): Caminho do arquivo CSV de entrada, lido com ``pd.read_csv``. output_csv (str): Caminho onde salvar o arquivo CSV filtrado, gravado sem o índice. O diretório pai já deve existir -- o pandas gera ``OSError`` em vez de criá-lo. column_name (str): Coluna à qual as duas comparações são aplicadas. Um nome que não está no quadro de dados gera ``KeyError``, e uma coluna de texto gera ``TypeError`` ao ser comparada com um limiar numérico. upper_threshold (float): As linhas estritamente maiores que este valor são mantidas. lower_threshold (float): As linhas estritamente menores que este valor também são mantidas; tudo o que fica entre os dois limites é descartado.

records.translation: O pivô é ``iinfo.min + iinfo.max``, que é o máximo do dtype para todo dtype sem sinal e ``-1`` para um com sinal, a mesma convenção usada por :func:`skimage.util.invert`. records.context: Migrate ``png_list``'s ``'o<N>'`` text ids onto the integer object label.
records.label: spacr.utils.object_label_from_png_id#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Migrate ``png_list``'s ``'o<N>'`` text ids onto the integer object label.
records.translation: Migra, em ``png_list``, os ids de texto ``'o<N>'`` para o rótulo inteiro do objeto.

records.context: ``png_list`` stores an object id as **text** (``'o5'``) because it is the last component of ``prcfo``; every object table stores the same object as an **integer** ``object_label``, and the child tables store their parent as an integer (in practice a float, since ``measure`` writes NaN for "no overlapping cell") ``cell_id``. Two types for one identity, which is why a plain SQL ``png_list.cell_id = nucleus.cell_id`` matches **zero rows** rather than failing: SQLite compares a TEXT value with an INTEGER one by type class, and text always sorts after numbers.
records.label: spacr.utils.object_label_from_png_id#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``png_list`` stores an object id as **text** (``'o5'``) because it is the last component of ``prcfo``; every object table stores the same object as an **integer** ``object_label``, and the child tables store their parent as an integer (in practice a float, since ``measure`` writes NaN for "no overlapping cell") ``cell_id``. Two types for one identity, which is why a plain SQL ``png_list.cell_id = nucleus.cell_id`` matches **zero rows** rather than failing: SQLite compares a TEXT value with an INTEGER one by type class, and text always sorts after numbers.
records.translation: ``png_list`` armazena um id de objeto como **texto** (``'o5'``) porque ele é o último componente de ``prcfo``; todas as tabelas de objetos armazenam o mesmo objeto como um ``object_label`` **inteiro**, e as tabelas filhas armazenam seu pai como inteiro (na prática, um float, já que ``measure`` grava NaN para "no overlapping cell") em ``cell_id``. Dois tipos para uma única identidade, e é por isso que um simples ``png_list.cell_id = nucleus.cell_id`` em SQL corresponde a **zero linhas** em vez de falhar: o SQLite compara um valor TEXT com um INTEGER pela classe de tipo, e texto sempre é ordenado depois de números.
